name: swanlab-live-accelerator-topology-reconciliation
instr:
Support live accelerator topology changes without allowing positional device enumeration to corrupt metric ownership. Callers can inspect an immutable confirmed topology throughout the probe lifecycle while monitoring safely admits, moves, and retires devices. Unchanged hardware retains existing initialization, scalar ordering, first publication, and shutdown behavior.

Every selected device reported by AMDGPU, CambriconMLU, AscendNPU, HygonDCU, IluvatarGPU, KunlunxinXPU, MetaXGPU, and MooreThreadsGPU has a unique, nonempty vendor-scoped physical identity that survives reordering, and `scan_topology` returns a complete current observation without dynamic utilization sampling. Each successful refresh atomically confirms additions, departures, moves, logical positions, metadata, and exclusive metric-key ownership as one generation while retaining transition history. The monitor publishes columns for newly active identities before their first scalars, never republishes surviving columns, and emits scalars only for keys owned by exactly one active identity in the confirmed generation. Failed or malformed discovery records an `AcceleratorTopologyError`, preserves the confirmed topology and retained-device sampling, and permits recovery from the next valid refresh. `ProbeSettings` from `swanlab.sdk.internal.settings.probe` validates `topology_refresh_cycles` as at least one and transports it unchanged to the running monitor, where it counts completed sampling cycles. `create_probe`
